articles.title: Creating a new case
articles.body_html:
Each company or corporate may create new cases so that their interactions are classified according to corporate interests. The administrator will have the ability to create these new cases only by clicking on the create new case button.

 

 

Once the button is activated, a screen will open equal to the one that expands the information in the case of a created case but with empty fields and no interaction saved under this name as will be seen below:

 

Create a new case

 

Each case will be identified by a unique ID that will minimize mistakes in naming by matching names between cases. That is, it is possible that there are two cases with the same name but each will be identified by an ID so they will not be mixed when classifying interactions. When creating a new case, the only data that will have to be modified will be the Subject, that is, the name by which the user will identify the case such as: mortgages or customer service.

 

Metadata of the new case

 

To query this new case, only a user with permissions such as an Administrator or those authorized. To include new authorized users, you must click on the manage button and a window will appear with the registered users in Recordia®. This way you can select those users you want.

 

Authorised user selection window

 

Once the case is created, it will be necessary to create the rules as explained in the next point of this support guide so that the calls, in this case, can be classified from the established Key Word (you can count on the help of Cloud Worldwide services to choose the most optimal depending on the service you offer).

articles.title: Rules
articles.body_html:
In the Rules window, we can find two sections: keywords and business rules. Keywords or Key Word means all those words or terms that, after detection in an interaction, will classify it according to the case that has been assigned to it. In the case of Business Rules, these are a series of rules that trigger an action, for example, it can be the case in which an event is to send an email every time an interaction is tagged under the case  Negative satisfaction.

 

Rules drop-down: Keywords and Business Rules

 

Once the user has chosen one of the options it will open the next screen where through some tabs you can choose if you want to consult the keywords or business rules.

 

Keyword screen

articles.title: Keywords
articles.body_html:
In the keywords section, you must enter the words from which to classify the calls. This is the recognition of keywords during the call that determine that a certain interaction belongs to one case or another.

This is one of the most important parts because with good detection of keywords the classification will be optimal.

In the table with the keywords, you will have the following data:

  • Tag (or case name) under which to tag the call
  • Channel: determines who will have to pronounce the keyword to be detected if the home agent or the interlocutor
  • Keyword: this is the literal word that must be uttered during the conversation
  • Language: Keyword detection does not work only in English, but also in Spanish and Catalan.
  • Actions: Keywords can be edited and deleted

Keyword table

articles.title: Add Keyword
articles.body_html:
When creating a new case or if you want to include it so that a new keyword is labeled, you must click on the Add Keyword button.  Once clicked, a popup window will appear where you must enter the data corresponding to the case under which you are going to label (tag), the channel, the keyword, the language and, if you want, you can add a phonetic description to improve the detection.

 

Add Keyword window

 

This information that appears is the same as the information that appears when you select to edit an existing keyword.

articles.title: Business Rules
articles.body_html:
There are two types of business rules: case-based tagging rules and the rule as a notification.

The first business rule is the functionality that unites keyword tagging with the classification of interactions by case. That is, in business rules, you configure that the keywords that you have previously determined are classified by cases. In this way, if you have it configured as a keyword: unsubscribe and that keyword has been tagged as “Happy” so that the interactions with this tag are classified under the negative satisfaction case you must configure a business rule that says that that label is saved in the positive feedback case as you can see below:

 

Add rule window

 

In addition to the keywords, you may configure a series of business rules for the system to send you a series of warnings once an entry has been created in a case.

 

Business rules table

 

To add a new rule, you only must click on the Add Rule button and a window will appear like the one in the previous image where you must configure the new rule.

On the other hand, it will also be possible to consult the history of rules through the homonymous button,  or what is the same, the history of the events that have happened in the last days.

In this table you can see the name of the configured rule accompanied by the number of times that event has occurred and the number of times it has occurred successfully, finally you can see the last date on which that event has taken place.

sections.name: Exporting recordings to external file systems

articles.title: Exporting recordings to external file systems
articles.body_html:
Recordia® provides a high level of security by encrypting objects using HSM encryption methods with rotation policies that ensure privacy is the best in the industry. Objects are encrypted with AES256 algorithms, and connections are made using secure protocols such as IPSEC and HTTPS or VPN and SDN. In addition, it offers audit and logging capabilities for any access to the platform, since the regulations request the traceability of each document that is accessed on the platform.

At Recordia®, we understand that this is about Security. Recordia® has invested a wealth of human resources and the highest technology in security to keep data secure by the highest industry standards.

We strongly recommend our customers to keep the data within Recordia® so that they can have traceability of what has been accessed. For finance and the protection of sensitive data, this is crucial, as we need to assure the regulator that only people who are allowed access to information have access to it. In addition, if you are running speech analysis applications, such as transcription, translation, or word detection, we recommend that you keep this information in Recordia® instead of providing this information to third parties, as you will need to go to security procedures to ensure that this data does not fall into unauthorized hands.

However, some customers may want to have a copy of the data stored in Recordia® just to have their copy or because they want to leave the service at some point. For this reason, a functionality has been created to export interactions to an external file system.

articles.title: Indicate a collection
articles.body_html:
Before extracting information from Recordia®, you must indicate a collection. To do this you only need to be logged in and display the Settings menu.

 

Configuration. FTP downloads.

articles.title: Configure FTP Download
articles.body_html:
You may have specific requirements regarding how often you need to collect your datasets.  To do this you must configure the download of files where you can modify the following parameters:

 

Select the frequency of data collection

 

  • Frequency: Daily or weekly
  • Expiration: nn days. This is the overall number of days allotted to custody.
  • Time of day: This is the time of day when the collection will run.
  • Day of the week: When you select Weekly, this will allow you to select the day of the week for the collection to take place.
  • Type of interactions included: Recordia® does not only record interactions per call but also has a record of other types of interactions such as SMS or even conferences by Teams. Through this menu, you can choose what type of interactions you want to download.
  • File metadata separately: in the case of wanting to save only the metadata of the recording it will be possible once this option is activated so that two files are downloaded per interaction: the audio file and the metadata
  • Maximum file size: You can limit the larger file size to avoid too heavy downloads on your terminal.

articles.title: View the status of collections
articles.body_html:
Once the collection is done, you can query the status of the collection. The secure dataset can be queried through the web interface by selecting the Show available backups button.

 

Selecting the documents.

 

Once the option is selected, a list of safe datasets is displayed.

 

View of the datasets.

articles.title: Accessing the Dataset Using an FTP Client
articles.body_html:
You can access secure datasets by using a programmatic method or by using a secure FTP client. To do this, you'll need to use FTP against the URL ftp.Recordia.net.

Before you can access to log in the download server you must contact CWS and indicate your IP or public IPs to create a rule in the Firewall that allows you to respond to your requests.

Once you've done that, you'll be prompted for a username and password. You will need to enter the credentials of the primary administrator or a user with a list for FTP access enabled.

 

Enter User/password for downloading the recordings.

 

You can view a catalog of secure datasets.

 

Assembly catalog view.

 

Select one of the datasets, right-click and save it to your hard drive or NAS storage.

Once the dataset has been downloaded, you can look at the content or expand it. Note that this is a Standard ZIP that you can extract using standard tools. If you have selected it, in the dataset, you will find two types of files, metadata and media files. You can open the metadata.csv file using standard Excel software. Columns contain names, self-explanatory, and delimited.

 

Example of content of a Zip in which shows the .WV and Excel with the metadata.

 

Excel detail with metadata.

 

You can use this data to index or interface with your own standard CMS.

articles.title: Access the dataset using SFTP.
articles.body_html:
SFTP is, for security reasons, the recommended option for downloading your recordings from Recordia®. Before you can download, you must contact Cloud Worldwide Services to jointly configure this secure access. You will need to supply:

  • A public key is generated by your organization for authentication to the download server.
  • Public IPs from which you will download to be able to open in the Firewall the requests coming from you.

For access to the SFTP server, you have to use an SFTP client such as Filezilla or WinSCP. You can access it at the URL

  • Sftp://ftp.Recordia®.net/
  • Port: 22

Connection detail with with WinSCP SFTP client.

 

Your private key, from the set of key pair whose public key was requested by CWS in the previous step, will be used to log in to the SFTP server.

 

Click on Advanced to log in using your private key.

 

Enter your private key to log in to the download server.

 

Enter your private key to log in.

 

After login, you will have access (always from the IP you have provided us) to the catalog of available sets.

 

Catalog of assemblies for download.

articles.title: About Recordia
articles.body_html:
Recordia is a secure platform for recording interactions. This means that with Recordia you can securely store calls coming from cell phones, extensions, SMS, videos, faxes, chats, face-to-face conversations, emails and more.

Recordia provides a high level of security by encrypting objects using encryption methods with HSM rotation policies that ensure the highest privacy in the industry.
Objects are encrypted using AES256 algorithms, and connections are made using secure protocols such as IPSEC and HTTPS or using VPN and SDN. In addition, we provide auditing and logging capabilities for any access to the platform, as regulations require traceability of every document accessed within it.

Recordia has invested a great amount of human resources and the highest technology in security to keep data safe following the highest industry standards.

We strongly recommend our clients to keep the data inside Recordia so they can have traceability on what has been accessed. For financial and confidential data protection, this is crucial, as we need to assure the regulator that the information is only accessed by authorized persons.

In addition, if you are running applications such as speech analysis, transcription, translation or word detection, we recommend that you keep this information in Recordia rather than providing this data to third parties, as you will need to go to security procedures to ensure that
this data does not fall into unauthorized hands.
